children: The artificial intelligence boom is likely becoming increasingly unsustainable, Capital Economics says in a note. Earnings expectations have been stretched, the firm's economists say. High valuations and huge investment plans are based on assumptions about AI's future profitability that may prove too optimistic, they add. As investors become more skeptical about future returns, Capital Economics expects a significant correction in technology stocks followed by a slowdown in U.S. AI investment. The research firm expects the U.S. stock market to fall around 30% from peak to trough by end-2027. The economists also except a similar peak-to-trough drop in Taiwan and a 50% selloff in South Korea. (amanda.lee@wsj.com)
